summary: Timebounded forensic export: per-session sequencing, duplicate-suppression checks, and TLS cert-rotation proof for SIEM ingestion
description:
Issue summary:
Customer requests a timeboxed forensic export covering a 3-hour window (2026-02-28T22:00Z to 2026-03-01T01:00Z) for a specific tenant. They report duplicate events arriving in their SIEM after our webhook bridge, and they require: (a) per-session reconstruction with ordering guarantees, (b) a signed delivery manifest (HMAC/SHA256 per-batch) for chain-of-custody, and (c) proof of TLS client certificate rotation timestamps used by our forwarder during that window.

Impact:
- Arcadia uses these exports for regulatory investigation. Duplicate events and missing ordering block their forensic analysis and escalate to legal/compliance. They marked this P1 / Sev1.

Environment:
- Redwood prod-us-east, customer Arcadia (enterprise) using tenant-id: arcadia-prod-42.
- SIEM: Customer-side Splunk HEC endpoint behind mutual TLS.

Steps to reproduce / customer-provided reproduction notes:
1) Customer replayed webhook ingestion of events for a 1-hour subset and observed duplicate event_ids in Splunk for specific session_ids.
2) They observed gaps in ordering for long-running sessions (>30s between tokens) that should be sequenced by our resume token.
3) Customer exported TLS logs from their edge and noted our client cert presented at 2026-02-28T22:30Z but no rotation record was available from our manifest.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate events are present for ~0.3% of events in the sampled window. Duplicates cluster around peaks when our bridge retries (backpressure) and during a short spike on 2026-02-28T22:28-22:32Z.
- Exported webhook manifest (customer copy) only contains batch checksums but lacks signed resume tokens for per-session ordering.
- Customer requests an attestation of the client cert thumbprint(s) used by our forwarder during the target window and a signed manifest including resume tokens and per-event sequence numbers.

Expected behavior:
- Ordered, deduplicated sequence for each session with monotonic sequence numbers.
- Signed per-batch manifest (HMAC-SHA256) with resume tokens to allow deterministic reassembly.
- TLS client cert rotation proof including issuance timestamps and KID/thumbprint.

Attachments provided by customer:
- sample_splunk_dupes.csv (100 rows)
- webhook_bridge_logs_20260228-22.gz (truncated)
- customer_tls_capture.pcap

Customer asks: full export for 2026-02-28T22:00Z -> 2026-03-01T01:00Z, signed manifest with batch checksums, per-event sequence numbers and resume tokens, and TLS client cert rotation record for the forwarder that pushed to their HEC endpoint.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Arcadia (Jane Li, security@arcadia.com): We need a forensics bundle ASAP — legal has a 72-hour hold. We can provide an SFTP destination. Please include signed resume tokens so our replay is deterministic.

2026-03-01 - Support (Sofia Martinez): Acknowledged. Triage assigned to Ethan Cole for SRE investigation. Requesting SFTP details and whether they need pseudonymization or redactable IDs.
Action: Collect raw bridge logs, look for retry spikes and outgoing certificate details.

2026-03-02 - Engineering (Ethan Cole): Confirmed we saw a retry window matching customer timestamps. Scheduling immediate export job with highest priority. Need legal-approved SFTP details and confirmation if Arcadia accepts PKCS7 signed manifest or prefers HMAC-SHA256 per-batch.
Suggested: HMAC-SHA256 with rotating KEK and include key id in manifest.

2026-03-04 - Arcadia (Jane Li): HMAC-SHA256 acceptable. SFTP endpoint: sftp.arcadia-corp.com:/incoming/forensics/arcadia-prod-42/ (creds sent to secure channel). Please include cert thumbprints and issuance timestamps. We also require a short playbook for how we can replay into Splunk preserving ordering.

2026-03-07 - SRE (Nina Patel): Export job completed; initial artifact uploaded to customer SFTP. Noted cluster of retries at 22:28 corresponding to transient 524s from our bridge. Uploaded preliminary manifest (unsigned) for review. Will provide signed manifest after KEK rotation check and notarization step.
2026-03-08 - Support (Ethan Cole): Delivering final signed manifest and rotation proof. See resolution notes. Awaiting customer confirmation; leaving ticket open for 72h to confirm successful replay.
2026-03-08 - Arcadia (Jane Li): Confirmed receipt, replay validated — duplicates suppressed when using provided resume tokens and the HMAC manifest. Closing pending final audit statement.
investigation_notes:
Queried bridge logs: found ~18k outgoing webhook batches in the window. Retry amplification occurred when our internal upstream returned 524 on a subset of requests at 22:28.
SQL-ish query used: SELECT batch_id, retries, status, timestamp FROM webhook_bridge WHERE tenant='arcadia-prod-42' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-02-28T22:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-01T01:00:00Z' ORDER BY timestamp;

Hypothesis: duplicates come from in-flight batch retransmits where downstream ack was received but our bridge's state machine retried due to a late ACK / race. Need to validate per-event ack idempotency keys.
Action: correlate batch_id -> event_id -> downstream ack timestamp in Splunk export.

Found that resume tokens were not persisted on older bridge binary (v1.14.0) under heavy load due to an edge case in the local FIFO flush path. A fix in v1.14.2 patches resume-token checkpointing.
Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1426

TLS: forwarder client certs were rotated at 2026-02-28T22:30:15Z (thumbprint: A3:1F:7B:...). Issuance logged in our keystore rotation log. Need to include audit proof (timestamped cert chain and KMS attestation).
resolution_notes: Workaround delivered (2026-03-07): bulk export delivered to customer SFTP with a temporary dedupe flag they can enable during replay. Provided a replay playbook explaining how to ingest preserving sequence and apply server-side dedupe using the provided resume tokens.

Fix applied (2026-03-05): bridge binary v1.14.2 deployed to prod-us-east with resume-token checkpointing fix. Rollout notes: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 4h; no regressions observed.
Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1426

Signed deliverables (2026-03-08):
- Signed manifest (HMAC-SHA256) per-batch with KEK id: kek-2026-02-18
- Per-event CSV with monotonic sequence_number, event_id, session_id, batch_id, checksum
- TLS rotation proof: exported client cert chain PEM + CA chain + timestamped keystore rotation log entry signed by Redwood KMS (attestation statement included)
All artifacts uploaded to Arcadia SFTP and a notarized checksum file added to the manifest.

Follow-ups: (a) schedule a 1:1 replay run with Arcadia to validate long-running-session handling under load, (b) add an automated post-export verification step to include resume-token snapshots in future manifests, (c) include a KB article summarizing dedupe+replay best practices.
Status: Delivered to customer. Ticket will be closed after 72h confirmation of successful replay and acceptance of artifacts.
resolution: Partial fix deployed and artifacts delivered; awaiting customer acceptance. See resolution_notes for details.
notes: Preserve ticket for audit: attach signed KEK rotation ledger and cross-reference with SOC2 runbook. Recommended to add automated manifest signing to scheduled exports for enterprise tenants.
